title: AI-designed FtsZ-directed peptide tested in vitro on pan-drug-resistant isolates
summary: A sequence-space diffusion model generated ten FtsZ-directed binders; machine-learning triage, co-folding and molecular dynamics selected one lead, Combined111, which was produced in Bacillus subtilis (single band of about 11.1 kDa). Against one pan-drug-resistant isolate of each of seven species it gave larger inhibition zones than last-resort antibiotics for five of seven, by a mean of 4.81 mm, but not significantly (p = 0.074). Each zone is a single measurement, and the FtsZ mechanism is a hypothesis without direct binding data.
ai_technology: Sequence-space diffusion model for peptide design, with machine-learning triage, co-folding and molecular dynamics

evidence.tested: The purified peptide was tested for inhibition zones against seven pan-drug-resistant clinical isolates.
evidence.unknown: Minimum inhibitory concentrations, target engagement, resistance, toxicity and in vivo efficacy remain unestablished. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A diffusion model generated the peptide binders, and ML triage with co-folding and molecular dynamics selected the lead.
